questions.question_text:
Sort the following terms into 'erosion processes' or 'deposition processes'.

hydraulic action, longshore drift, corrasion, a wave losing energy and dropping material on a beach, formation of a spit, corrosion

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1: Categorise the coastal processes. (Note: longshore drift is transportation, but if strictly forced into two categories, it often groups with depositional features like spits, or should be identified as transportation).
keywords_required: Erosion processes: hydraulic action, corrasion, corrosion.
Deposition processes: a wave losing energy and dropping material on a beach, formation of a spit.
Transportation: longshore drift.

questions.question_text:
Decide if the following statements are true or false:
a) Swash carries sediment down the beach.
b) Longshore drift is influenced by the direction of prevailing winds.
c) Suspension involves large pebbles rolling along the seabed.

keywords_required: a) False (Swash carries sediment UP the beach; backwash carries it down).
b) True (Prevailing winds determine the angle waves hit the beach).
c) False (Suspension is fine material carried in the water; large pebbles rolling is traction).

questions.question_text: How does wave refraction help to form headlands and bays?

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2: Explain the role of wave refraction.
keywords_required: As waves approach a discordant coastline, the water gets shallower in front of the headland first.
This causes the wave to slow down, bend, and concentrate its energy on the headland, increasing erosion (forming cliffs/caves).
In the bay, the water is deeper, so the waves diverge and dissipate their energy.
This loss of energy leads to deposition in the bay, helping to form a beach.

questions.question_text: Produce a labelled diagram of a destructive wave, showing its main characteristics.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1: Characteristics of a destructive wave.
keywords_required: High wave height (amplitude) and steep wave.
Short wavelength and high frequency (10-15 per minute).
Weak swash and strong backwash.
Erodes the beach (plunging breaker).

questions.question_text: Describe how sediment is moved along the coast.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Describe the process of longshore drift.
keywords_required: Prevailing winds cause waves to approach the coast at an angle.
The swash carries sediment up the beach at this same angle.
The backwash carries sediment straight down the beach under the influence of gravity (at a right angle to the shoreline).
This creates a zig-zag movement of sediment along the beach.
This process is known as longshore drift.

questions.question_text: Study Figure 2.1. Describe the impacts of installing groynes on this coastline shown in Figure 2.1.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO3: Describe the visual impacts from the figure.
keywords_required: Sediment has built up on one side of the groyne (up-drift side).
This creates a wider, higher beach on that side.
On the other side of the groyne (down-drift side), there is less sand / the beach is narrower.
The groynes interrupt longshore drift, trapping sand.
This provides coastal protection by absorbing wave energy where the beach is wide.
